posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Button names should be strings, e.g.
JavaScript:
Input.isTriggered("ok")
I've used
ok
here instead of
z
because by default there is no button named
z
in the core scripts. The game input
ok
is triggered by several keys on the keyboard (space, enter, Z), as well as a gamepad button: pressing any of these will count as triggering
ok
in-game.
Also, in future if you want your thread moved you can just click the Report button on it. No need to clutter the place with duplicate threads.
[Edit: corrected
TouchInput
to
Input
.
]

I just realised I made a mistake in my previous post, re the plugin parameter. Try one of these instead:
Did touch input (mouse/touch) change from "not-pressed" to "pressed" this frame?
JavaScript:
TouchInput.isTriggered()
Did the OK button (keyboard/gamepad) change from "not-pressed" to "pressed" this frame?

Input.isTriggered("ok")
Are either of the above conditions true?
JavaScript:
TouchInput.isTriggered() || Input.isTriggered("ok")

posts.author: SGHarlekin
posts.body:
What's it supposed to register? You're starting the input sequence, meaning your variable 1 will increase by 1 every frame. You wait for this input for 60 frames and then stop the input. (btw you don't need the "end sequence input here, as the "wait for sequence input" already puts the variable at 0 if no input was registered, although it doesn't really hurt to have it either I suppose)
What you're doing is simply counting up a variable, but don't do anything with it. The sequence input is not a conditional branch on its own.
You have an "else", but no "if". You need to do something like:
Code:
if $gameVariables.value(1) <= 60
    do stuff (this is what should happen if input has been triggered within these 60 frames)
else
   do stuff (this is what should happen if the player fails the input)

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body: Like SGHarlekin said, but since the variable will be 0 if you didn't press anything, so you shouldn't check <= 60 (which is true for zero), but instead > 0
